title: UTF-16 terminated code-unit length
summary: Recovered the read-only cdecl scan at 0x425bc0 from accepted assembly and direct Game.exe disassembly. Counts 16-bit units through the first zero, excludes the terminator, and preserves the original 32-bit subtraction/arithmetic-shift result. The direct caller at 0x425ece supplies a string pointer and uses signed length comparisons.
test_description: Differential original-reference comparisons for all lengths 0 through 4096 at a two-byte-offset address, plus embedded byte zeros, surrogate pairs, lone surrogates, noncharacters, immediate terminators and trailing nonzero data. Assert expected code-unit lengths and compare all 4100 input/guard units after both calls for absence of writes.
known_limits: Requires readable storage through the first zero; null, inaccessible and unterminated inputs are not executed in tests and have no recovery error policy.
Address-wrapping scans are outside portable C++ object semantics. Huge sign-bit byte distances are preserved algebraically but not allocated or exercised.
Behavioral validation does not establish matching machine code or recover the surrounding caller.
